title: FuseMax: Leveraging Extended Einsums to Optimize Attention Accelerator Design
problem: Attention accelerators suffer from load imbalance between operators causing compute under-utilization, and on-chip buffer requirements that scale with sequence length. Prior work reduces memory bandwidth but fails to address these fundamental architectural bottlenecks.
motivation: Attention is a critical transformer workload increasingly targeted for custom acceleration, requiring designs that achieve high compute utilization and eliminate sequence-length dependent memory scaling.
method: The paper leverages Einsum cascades abstraction to formally describe and classify attention algorithms, enabling derivation of lower bounds on input data passes with implications for buffer and bandwidth requirements. FuseMax maps attention onto a spatial array-style architecture using novel binding strategies that achieve near-perfect compute utilization independent of sequence length.
key_novelty: Using cascade of Einsums as a formal abstraction to characterize attention algorithm space and derive lower bounds on required on-chip buffer capacity or memory traffic.
contributions: Einsum cascade framework for formalizing and taxonomizing attention algorithms
Lower bound analysis on kernel passes through data with buffer/bandwidth implications
FuseMax architecture achieving 100% compute utilization with sequence-length-independent memory
6.7x speedup over FLAT on attention (iso-area); 5.3x speedup on full transformer inference
primary_theme: formal characterization of attention algorithms via einsum cascades for accelerator optimization
